rows: The Andrews County Sheriff's Office reported golfball size hail falling 12 miles north of Andrews.
Hail up to the size of pennies was reported from near Florey to Frankel City.
Pea to nickel size hail was reported from just northwest of Andrews to just southwest of the intersection of Texas Highway 176 and Farm to Market Road 1788.

The Andrews County Sheriff's Office reported damage and one injury due to severe thunderstorm winds just southeast of Andrews. Observations from the West Texas Mesonet station in Andrews reported a maximum wind gust of 55 mph. The injured person had been hit in the face and chest…
Some leaves were stripped from trees northwest of Andrews as a result of penny size hail.
Penny to golfball sized hail fell in Andrews.
A tornado was reported by a person that viewed it through binoculars at a location 25 miles east of the tornado. The tornado lasted for five minutes.
Tennis ball sized hail fell on the west side of Andrews.

Powerlines and trees were downed by strong winds. A roof was also blown off a building and onto powerlines.
Trained spotters estimated winds of 60 mph on the Ector/Andrews county line. No damage was reported.
Several powerlines were downed by strong winds in the city of Andrews.
The Texas Tech Mesonet station east of Andrews reported a thunderstorm wind gust of 68 mph. No damage was reported.

Silver dollar sized hail damaged home windows near the intersection of County Road 2001 and Texas State Highway 176.
No damage was reported with this event.
Law enforcement reported powerlines were downed by strong winds in Andrews, TX.

A land owner reported that a 4 foot tree was blown over and several 4 to 5 inch tree limbs were broken. In addition, the roof of a 30' by 50' barn was torn off and some of the home's roof shingles were damaged.
Quarter sized hail occurred just west of the intersection of FM 3901 and SH 176. Cotton crop damage was reported, but the acreage was unknown.

A thunderstorm moved over Andrews County and produced a 70 mph wind gust five miles south southwest of Frankel City. These winds blew a telephone pole down on a car. The cost for the damage is a rough estimate.

A severe thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a tornado about an eighth of a mile east of Frankle City, TX. A National Weather Service employee spotted the damage at about 9:30 PM CDT. The damage consisted of one power pole bent at a 60 degree angle to the south …
A thunderstorm moved over Andrews County and produced a 70 mph wind gust that knocked down telephone poles 0.25 miles east of Frankel City. The cost of the damage is an estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a strong wind gust which resulted in several trees and power lines being blown down. This wind gust is estimated to have been around 70 mph, and the cost of damage from the wind is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved over Andrews County and produced a 61 mph wind gust two miles east of Andrews.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced an estimated 45 mph wind gust. This wind had blown off the roof of a structure. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 58 mph wind gust near the town of Andrews. No damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 58 mph wind gust near the City of Andrews.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 62 mph wind gust at the City of Andrews AWOS site.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 62 mph wind gust two miles east of Andrews.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced wind damage eight miles south of the City of Andrews. A few telephone poles were blown down. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A storm moved over Andrews County and produced quarter sized hail which covered the road at the intersection of US 385 and County Road SE 6000.

A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced tennis ball sized hail six miles east of Andrews. Windows in vehicles were broken from the hail. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced a 58 mph wind gust near Andrews.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 62 mph wind gust near the town of Andrews.
A thunderstorm moved across Andrews County and produced a 67 mph wind gust near the town of Andrews.
A thunderstorm produced 2.50 inch hail five miles west southwest of Andrews, TX. There was damage to car windshields. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to golf ball size 15 miles south of Frankel City. There were accumulated hail piles several inches deep and covering the road.
Two-inch hail was observed along Ranch Rd 181.
Quarter-size hail was reported via mPing.
This report was received from mPing.
The Mesonet station 48 2E Andrews recorded a 60 mph wind gust.
The AWOS station KE11 Andrews measured a 58 mph wind gust. The total time/duration of occurrence is estimated (partially based on the Andrew's Mesonet station measurement).
Law enforcement at the Andrews Police Department measured 1.25 inch hail. The time of occurrence is estimated by radar.

A video was shared by the public on social media of nickel to quarter-size hail covering the side of the road and in grassy areas along FM 2371 west of Andrews. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar.
